name: Reef Line and Karst Isles
inspired_by: The eastern South China Sea as of 2026: a Palawan-type island of limestone karst, rainforest, mangroves and stilt fishing villages on the east of the map, and a Spratly-type reef group to the west with a grounded-ship outpost, small occupied islets of several claimants, an artificial island base, and an offshore gas platform. Coast guard water-cannon and blocking incidents, maritime militia swarms and resupply runs to outposts define the confrontation. All towns and features are fictional.
climate: Tropical monsoon (Koppen Am). 26-33 C year-round, very humid. South-west monsoon (habagat) June-October with heavy rain and typhoons in the north; north-east monsoon (amihan) December-March, drier with steady winds and rough seas on exposed reefs. 1,500-3,000 mm rain.
seasons: Amihan (Dec-Mar): drier, steady north-east winds, rough water on the reefs
Hot dry (Apr-May): calm seas, best for resupply runs and exercises
Habagat (Jun-Oct): heavy rain, squalls, typhoon events, poor visibility

vegetation: none (water): deep blue sea, turquoise lagoons
coral reefs exposed at low tide
coconut palms and beach almond on the shore

terrain.relief: East: a long narrow island with a mountain spine to 1,100 m, karst towers and cliffs on the west coast, coastal plains and mangrove bays on the east coast. West: open sea up to 1,500 m deep with atolls and reefs rising from it; reef tops at 0-2 m, sand cays 1-4 m above high tide; one artificial island of dredged sand at 3-6 m with a runway.
features: a reef shoal with a grounded rusting ship used as an outpost
an artificial island with seawalls, runway and radar domes
small occupied islets with concrete outpost buildings
terrain.water: Sea covers most of the map; island rivers short and steep with estuaries; lagoons inside atolls; tide exposes reef flats.

generator.approach: Heightmap with bathymetry at 20 m (sea) and 10 m (island). Island as an elongated mask with ridged noise spine and karst towers from cellular noise; deep sea from low-frequency noise; atolls as ring shapes (annulus SDF) rising from depth with lagoons; cays and the artificial island stamped. Tide variable for reef exposure.

noise_layers.purpose: karst towers on the west coast
atolls rising from depth to reef level

generator.erosion: Hydraulic erosion on the island spine; karst towers keep vertical walls (thermal cap 80 degrees).
generator.rivers: Short steep island rivers by flow accumulation, ending in mangrove estuaries.
generator.settlement_flattening: Coastal villages on beach ridges and stilts over water; town on the bay plain; outposts on cays and reef platforms.
generator.notes: Most play is maritime: boats, boarding, resupply runs, small-island actions. Typhoon events close the sea. Grey-zone incidents (water cannon, blocking, ramming) are scripted vessel behaviours, not shooting.

settlements.architecture: Fishing villages: houses on stilts over water and on the beach, of wood and woven bamboo (sawali) with nipa thatch or corrugated-iron roofs, plank walkways, outrigger bancas pulled up on the sand; a chapel or small mosque, a basketball court, sari-sari stores.
layout_rules: along the shore and over the water on stilts
basketball court and chapel at the centre

settlements.architecture: Municipal town: two- and three-storey concrete and cinder-block buildings with corrugated roofs and balconies, a Spanish-era church plaza, a municipal hall, a public market, a port with fishing and ferry piers, tricycle stands.
settlements.wall_class: Cinder block medium; wood upper floors thin.
layout_rules: plaza with church and municipal hall
national highway as the main street

settlements.architecture: Outposts and bases: the grounded-ship outpost (rusting hull with shacks on deck), small-islet outposts of concrete buildings with flags, a lighthouse and a helipad, the artificial-island base (hangars, radar domes, seawalls, runway), a naval/coast guard station in a bay, an offshore gas platform (steel decks), a Taiwanese-held island garrison at the far west edge.
settlements.wall_class: Concrete outposts thick; ship hull steel (thin-medium); platform steel.
layout_rules: each outpost on a different reef or cay
the artificial island at the far west of the reef group
coast guard station in the main island's bay

settlements.architecture: Coconut and cashew plantation homesteads, seaweed farms on stakes in shallow bays with drying platforms.

infrastructure.roads: One national highway along the island's east coast, dirt roads inland; nothing on the reefs.
infrastructure.power: Diesel plants and solar on the island; outposts on generators.
infrastructure.ports: Town port with ferry and fishing piers, coast guard station, outrigger landings; the artificial island's harbour; the LHD offshore east of the reefs.
infrastructure.airfields: Town airport (domestic), the artificial island's runway (AI only), an islet airstrip.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Coast guard at the port; none on the reefs; blocking lines of coast guard and militia vessels near shoals (events).

pois.description: Rusting grounded ship on a shoal used as an outpost: deck shacks, a small garrison, a helipad, resupply only by boat through blocking vessels.
Dredged island base: seawalls, runway, hangars, radar domes, missile shelters, harbour. Observe only.
pois.contract_use: reconnaissance from a boat; late-game escalation objective

pois.description: Small cay with a concrete outpost building, flag, lighthouse, solar panels and a jetty; a few soldiers.
Offshore gas platform with decks, cranes, a helideck and accommodation module.
pois.contract_use: protect infrastructure (offshore oil platforms) (client vnm or phl); boarding

pois.description: Dozens of large fishing vessels anchored in a reef lagoon in rows, rarely fishing.
pois.contract_use: maritime security observation; document for a client

pois.description: Fishing village on stilts with plank walkways and bancas; fishermen harassed at the shoals.
pois.contract_use: escort fishermen; disaster relief security after a typhoon

pois.description: Hidden cove under karst cliffs with a sea cave, used by smugglers.
Coast guard station with pier, patrol boats, a radar mast and barracks.
pois.contract_use: contract board; maritime security boarding staging

pois.description: Crashed surveillance drone on a reef flat, accessible at low tide.
pois.contract_use: recover before rival vessels (clients phl, usa, jpn)

pois.description: Coastal town after a typhoon: roofs torn off, flooded streets, relief goods at the plaza.
pois.contract_use: disaster relief security (clients phl, aus, nzl, jpn)

pois.description: Small island with a runway, hospital, port and garrison at the west edge.
Grass airstrip in the rainforest with a hangar shed, used by a logging company and smugglers.

weather.visibility_notes: Squalls drop visibility to under 500 m and ground helicopters; typhoons shut everything; jungle limits sight to 10-30 m; sea glare.

civilians.behaviour: Fishermen out at night with lights and back at dawn; markets at the town pier in the morning; Sunday church; basketball in the evening. At sea, fishing bancas work near the shoals and are harassed by larger vessels. Typhoon events send people to evacuation centres (schools, churches).
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Fishing boats near incidents and dense stilt villages are the main risks.

factions_present.where: The main island, coast guard station, grounded-ship outpost and one islet; navy and coast guard patrols.
Artificial island base, coast guard cutters and maritime militia swarms around the reefs (grey zone).
One islet outpost and the gas platform sector in the south-west.
Garrison island at the far west edge.
Advisers at the coast guard station, maritime patrol aircraft, exercises (EDCA-type site on the main island).
Coast guard patrol vessel donations, observers and joint exercises.
Joint patrols and exercises; disaster relief teams.

frontline: Maritime grey zone. Control of each shoal is a state (open, contested, blocked). chn blocking and water-cannon events raise contest levels and make resupply runs harder; successful runs and allied patrols lower them. Islets do not change hands in the default state. Typhoon events pause the confrontation and post relief contracts. The late-game escalation scenario (proposed) puts the outposts under blockade and assault.
contract_hooks: Resupply the grounded-ship outpost through a blocking line (client phl)
Reconnaissance of the Spratly-type reefs (clients phl, vnm)
Protect the offshore gas platform (client vnm)
Maritime security boarding of a smuggling vessel (client phl)
Hostage rescue from a kidnap gang in a karst cove (client phl)
Recover a downed drone from a reef at low tide (clients phl, usa, jpn)
Disaster relief security after a typhoon (clients phl, aus, nzl, jpn)
Escalation scenario: hold an islet outpost (late game)

hot_zones.name: Reef group escalation (late game)
hot_zones.layout: chn HQ on the artificial island; 3-4 occupied reefs as outposts; blocking lines as checkpoints; roaming cutters and militia vessels; QRF by boat and helicopter; friendly islet outposts as anchors

insertion.fob: LHD east of the reef group; FOB at the coast guard station on the main island. Boats, helicopters and AAVs (lagoons and beaches).

early_game_notes: The main confrontation is with chn (late tier). phl's early-game counter-terror hook (ISIS-affiliated cells on southern islands) needs isis to list this theatre (open question); until then only criminal kidnap gangs (generic NPCs) appear.

shoal control states and blocking-vessel behaviour
